_about: Hard Hat Mack, Electronic Arts, 1983. A 42,112-byte .COM written by
hand: no compiler prologue anywhere in it, and no library, so
probelib.py finds nothing -- 0 of 250 entry points, which is a real
negative result rather than a failure.
It keeps its variables next to the code that uses them. 436 addresses
fall into 132 clusters scattered through the image, and the two that
carry most of the traffic are the actor block at 0x0B60 (391
references in 0x21 bytes) and the drawing block at 0x6D97 (789 in
This file is honest about being unfinished. The routines named below
were read; the 180-odd that were not are listed in _unread with what
the profiler could see about each, and none of them has been given a

0x0004: CS everywhere, INT 09h hooked through 0:0x24 with the old vector kept at 0x0782, the BIOS equipment word forced to 40-column colour, mode 4, and five added to all 200 scanline_table entries before anything is drawn
0x0060: the same video setup without the vector work
0x0071: reads port 0x60, maps the scan code through scan_map, and keeps any entry with the high bit set in key_pressed. Two mapped values are not keys at all: 1 unhooks the vector and returns far to DOS, 2 jumps to the configuration menu
0x00DF: AL times AL of nothing; the only timing the game has
0x00EA: stops the tone generator and biases BL by 0x80
0x0105: port 0x201 bit 0x10 rotated into the carry through AH
0x0123: 0x50 bytes of AL along every one of the 200 scanlines, five bytes in from where scanline_table points -- which is what the five added at start-up is for
0x013E: turns (place_col, place_row) into a screen address: seven bytes to a column, the row through row_table, and the low two bits of the column kept as a shift
0x0199: the inner loop of the three place_ routines
0x01C8: the rectangle filler: rows fill_row0 to fill_row1, columns fill_col0 to fill_col1, fill_step deciding whether rows advance by one or two
0x0217: multiplies place_col by seven, takes place_row as it stands, and draws shape_select. Forty-seven callers -- the busiest routine in the program
0x0268: two shapes at unit column scale
0x02B1: two shapes at the seven-pixel column scale
0x036D: what all three placement routines reach
0x096B: loads a divisor and gates the speaker
0x09B5: programs PIT channel 0 through ports 0x43 and 0x40 -- the only place the tick rate is set
0x0F49: the actor loop, 430 instructions over 79 blocks: state, timer, direction and frame for every actor in the actor block, and the four movement routines it dispatches to
0x11F6: actor_x and actor_y into a place_pair
0x14D8: one screen: the girders through fill_tiles, then the ladders, the hazards, the rivets, and the actors, dispatched on screen_number through mode_vector
0x1627: the same shape for the second screen layout
0x1841: three fill_tiles calls with shapes 0xBD, 0xBE and 0xBF -- the three-row girder every screen stands on
0x1A7E: a horizontal run of one shape
0x1CEA: one actor's position by its velocity pair
0x2169: sets up a screen: seventeen reads of key_pressed while it waits, the state vector, the hazard table, and the actor block
0x2428: the six-byte hazard record at hazard_slots
0x3A8F: adds to the five-digit score at score_digits and redraws it, then queues the scoring sound through music_push
0x45FB: saves the tune position so a sound effect can take the speaker and give it back. Sixteen callers, every one of them an event that makes a noise. It was called shift_history
0x4648: back to the default tune at tune_default
0x4661: the software synthesiser. Adds the note's phase increment to the accumulator 0x78 times a tick and toggles port 0x61 bit 1 against a duty threshold that itself drifts -- pulse-width modulation on a one-bit speaker

0x0103: the keyboard ISR refuses to return to DOS unless this is set
0x052D: 200 words, one per scanline: 0x0000, 0x2000, 0x0050, 0x2050 -- the two CGA banks interleaved. Start-up adds five to every entry, so the playfield begins five bytes in and clear_playfield writes 0x50 bytes from there
0x072D: 0x80 bytes: scan code to game action. Values 1 and 2 are the two escapes, anything with the high bit set is a movement key
0x0781: what the ISR left; cleared by whoever consumes it
0x0782: the vector the ISR puts back on the way out
0x0786: the PSP segment, saved so the far return has one
0x0B60: 99 references; also the first byte of the 0x21-byte actor block that runs to 0x0B80
0x0BD9: `jmp word [0x0BD9]`; comrec resolves it to 0x0BB6 by following what writes it
0x15B1: non-zero makes rows advance in twos
0x1B64: the five flags place_sprite tests, 129 references
0x2500: six bytes, one per hazard on the screen
0x46F5: where music_push keeps the interrupted position
0x46F7: how fast the pulse width drifts
0x46F8: the tune music_reset goes back to
0x4895: phase increments, two bytes a note
0x5A2A: five digits, one per byte, 45 references
0x6D97: 0, 768, 1024, 1280, 3072, 3328 -- multiples of 256, so an index into a shape table
0x6D9B: the column; place_sprite multiplies it by seven
0x6D9C: the row, used as it stands
0x6D9D: the second shape's, in the pair routines
0x6DC3: how long this note still has
0x6DC8: 111 references, read and written by one cluster
0x6DDA: the note stream position. It was called input_latch
0x726B: read by three routines, written by none
0x726F: what locate_cell turns a row into

_note: File offsets, contiguous across the whole 42,112-byte image.
Hard Hat Mack has no separate data segment: 19,719 bytes are data
and 5,394 of those are scattered in 646 runs shorter than 64
bytes, sitting between the routines that own them.
0x00000: the entry, the keyboard ISR, the three placement routines and the two blitters
0x005BD: the configuration text and the scan code map
0x008DE: the tone generator, the timer, and the first actor code
0x00F03: a 70-byte table of word pairs the actor loop indexes
0x00F49: the actor loop, the level drawing and the fill primitive
0x01FE8: the hazards and the rivet logic
0x0251A: 1,171 bytes of shape rows -- runs of 0x54 and the ascending ladders
0x029AD: the per-object placement helpers, one short routine each
0x02F36: 565 bytes of descending and ascending byte ramps: the girder and ladder column patterns
0x0316B: the score, the four screens' hazards, the bonus
0x0394C: the screen scripts, the collision checks, and the music player
0x04837: the remaining screen scripts and the actor variants
0x0648A: the last of the code, ending where the shape data begins
0x06C8B: 14,325 bytes of shape data, 42% zero. Every sprite in the game, and the working variables the drawing code keeps at 0x6D97..0x6DC9 sit at the front of it

_unread: 180 of the 221 call targets have not been read instruction by
instruction. Most are short and follow one of two shapes: set
place_col, place_row and shape_select and call place_sprite (about
sixty of them), or set a level pointer and fall into the shared game
loop (about a dozen entries that all reach the same 350-instruction
tail, which is why the profiler reports them at that size).
They are left unnamed deliberately. Naming a routine `draw_shape_12`
from its constants would raise the count without adding a fact, and
the count is not the point.
